sentences.en: Excuse me, can you help me?
I am trying to find the library.
Is it far from here?
It is about ten minutes away.
Should I walk or take a taxi?
sentences.ar: هل الأفضل أن أمشي أم أركب سيارة أجرة؟

sentences.en: Walking is faster at this time.
Go straight ahead.
Turn left at the next street.
Take the second right.
sentences.ar: انعطف عند ثاني شارع إلى اليمين.

sentences.en: Cross at the traffic lights.
The building is on your right.
It is next to the pharmacy.
Look for the blue sign.
You cannot miss the entrance.
sentences.ar: لن تخطئ في العثور على المدخل.

sentences.en: Is there a shortcut?
The shortcut goes through the park.
Be careful at that intersection.
Is the station nearby?
The station is across the road.
sentences.ar: المحطة على الجانب الآخر من الطريق.

sentences.en: Could you show me on the map?
sentences.ar: هل يمكنك أن تريني على الخريطة؟

sentences.en: My phone has lost the signal.
Let me check the street name.
I think we passed the turn.
We need to go back one block.
sentences.ar: علينا العودة مسافة مربع سكني واحد.

sentences.en: Is this the correct entrance?
The main entrance is around the corner.
How do I get to the parking area?
Follow the signs downstairs.
The elevator is behind you.
Take the stairs to the first floor.
Thank you for the clear directions.
You are very welcome.
I found the place easily.
Next time I will know the way.

sections.heading: A new situation
paragraphs: Dina was learning how to handle asking for directions in everyday English. The goal was to communicate clearly and politely. Dina practiced “Excuse me, can you help me?” A useful phrase was “I am trying to find the library.” A useful phrase was “Is it far from here?” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “It is about ten minutes away.” A useful phrase was “Should I walk or take a taxi?” A useful phrase was “Walking is faster at this time.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Go straight ahead.” A useful phrase was “Turn left at the next street.” A useful phrase was “Take the second right.” They repeated it to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Finding the right words
paragraphs: As the situation developed, Dina listened carefully and tried more useful expressions. Dina practiced “Cross at the traffic lights.” A useful phrase was “The building is on your right.” A useful phrase was “It is next to the pharmacy.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Look for the blue sign.” A useful phrase was “You cannot miss the entrance.” A useful phrase was “Is there a shortcut?” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “The shortcut goes through the park.” A useful phrase was “Be careful at that intersection.” A useful phrase was “Is the station nearby?” They repeated it to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Making a choice
paragraphs: There were more details to understand, so Dina slowed down and chose the next words thoughtfully. Dina practiced “The station is across the road.” A useful phrase was “Could you show me on the map?” A useful phrase was “My phone has lost the signal.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Let me check the street name.” A useful phrase was “I think we passed the turn.” A useful phrase was “We need to go back one block.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Is this the correct entrance?” A useful phrase was “The main entrance is around the corner.”

sections.heading: A confident finish
paragraphs: At the end of the activity, Dina reviewed the final expressions and felt more comfortable speaking. Dina practiced “How do I get to the parking area?” A useful phrase was “Follow the signs downstairs.” A useful phrase was “The elevator is behind you.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Take the stairs to the first floor.” A useful phrase was “Thank you for the clear directions.” A useful phrase was “You are very welcome.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “I found the place easily.” A useful phrase was “Next time I will know the way.”
